grades.reason: Back-of-book index fragment; it contains no explanation of page faults, permissions or missing mappings.
Mentions page-fault uses such as memory-mapped files and stack growth. It does not say how to tell a permission fault from a missing mapping.

grades.quote: xv6 maps the text without PTE_W; if a program accidentally attempts to store to address 0, the hardware will refuse to execute the store and raises a page fault
grades.reason: Gives examples of permission-caused page faults, such as a store to a text page mapped without PTE_W and access to a guard page with PTE_U cleared. It does not explain how to diagnose or distinguish them from a missing mapping.

grades.quote: PTE is invalid (i.e., PTE_V is not set), so that if the kernel overflows a kernel stack, it will likely cause a page fault
grades.reason: Contrasts an invalid PTE (PTE_V not set, i.e. no valid mapping) that causes a page fault with valid mappings restricted by R/W/X permission bits. This gives the conceptual basis for telling the two apart by inspecting the PTE. It does not describe fault-cause registers or a diagnostic procedure.
